# 3D Virtual Store

> A portfolio proof of concept by Michael Mas: a 3D showroom where visitors walk between pedestals, customize products (three glasses, a lipstick, a face paint) and try them on live with their webcam. Everything runs in the browser: WebGPU rendering with a WebGL2 fallback, face tracking with MediaPipe in WebAssembly, no server and no third-party requests.

- Source code and full technical write-up: https://github.com/michael-mas/3d-virtual-store
- Author: Michael Mas (https://github.com/michael-mas)

## Technical highlights

- Next.js App Router static export, TypeScript strict, deployed on Vercel.
- React Three Fiber on three.js `WebGPURenderer`; a single persistent canvas, modes swap scene content.
- Materials and post-processing written in TSL (three.js shading language): transmissive and iridescent lenses, holographic shaders, lipstick lit from the video's own luminance, neon face paint with additive halos.
- Try-on: MediaPipe Face Landmarker (478 landmarks, blendshapes) served locally; rigid products follow the facial transformation matrix with a head occluder; makeup is drawn on a face mesh rebuilt from the landmarks every frame, with masks authored in canonical-face UV space.
- Products are data: a registry entry defines attachment type, customization schema and pricing; the customizer UI and cart are generated from it.
- All 3D models are generated by code (glTF + Draco), including three procedural glasses frames.
- Quality: unit tests (Vitest), end-to-end tests (Playwright) running the full loop in CI, strict Content Security Policy, zero external runtime requests.
